prompt: The robot opens a special door only for door 3. What is printed?

options.text: `done`. The if is False, so its indented line is skipped.
options.feedback: Right. The indented line belongs to the if and runs only when its condition is True; the last line always runs.

options.text: `three` then `done`. The indented line always runs.
options.feedback: The if decides whether its indented line runs. Here door is 2, so the condition is False and three is not printed.

options.text: Nothing is printed. A False if stops the whole program, even after it.
options.feedback: A False if skips only its own indented line. The last line is not part of it, so done is printed.

options.text: `done`. Python never runs an indented line under an if.
options.feedback: Indented lines do run when the if is True. With door = 3 this program prints three, then done.
options.partial_reason: Correct: done. Incorrect: that indented lines never run; they run when their if is True.

explanation: door is 2, so door == 3 is False. The indented print("three") belongs to the if and is skipped. print("done") is not indented, so it runs and the program prints done.
